title: Operator Handoff and Telemetry Playbook for Private Deploy Cutovers
author: Marina Gomez
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the operational handoff and telemetry verification process for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem variants). It focuses on the operator-to-customer handoff during initial commissioning, model swap cutovers, and major runtime upgrades where evidence packages and telemetry continuity are required by compliance and SLAs. The document is intended for operator teams, SREs, customer field engineers, and solutions engineers responsible for commissioning and day-2 observability.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, audit-friendly handoff process that preserves traceability of configuration and evidence for regulated customers.
- Ensure telemetry continuity (no gaps > 5 minutes for critical signals) during cutovers and upgrades.
- Validate SLOs and regression checks before final signoff.
- Define rollback decision criteria and evidence-preservation steps.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to Private deployments (VPC-connected and air-gapped on-prem packages).
- Assumes runtime is Redwood inference runtime v3.x or later and operator has privileged access to the control plane and telemetry ingestion endpoints.
- Customer must provide network ACLs, KMS/HSM access patterns, and a pre-approved operator account per the Customer Handoff Checklist (section below).

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: Operator Field Services (team: eng-private-deployments/operators)
- Secondary owner: Runtime Observability (team: eng-platform/observability)
- On-call escalation: eng-sre PagerDuty (primary rotation)
- Field contact template: Name / Role / Phone / Pager / Slack handle

Acceptance criteria (pre-handoff)

Operators must achieve the following before initiating customer signoff: 

1. Infrastructure readiness verified: compute pools at >= 95% of targeted capacity, stable for 30 minutes.
2. Security controls verified: KMS integration tested (signature test), TLS certs valid and pinned.
3. Telemetry pipeline health: ingestion latency < 120s (95th), no more than 1% dropped events in prior 24h.
4. KV cache priming: model artifacts uploaded and warmed for representative prompt set.

Minimum telemetry signals and sampling policy

Table: Signal / Purpose / Retention / Sampling

- request.latency.p50, request.latency.p95, request.latency.p99 / latency SLO tracking / 90 days / full (no sampling)
- model.swap.event / model swap audit / 365 days / full
- kv.cache.hit_ratio / cache efficiency / 90 days / 1:1 for errors, 1:10 for successful requests
- runtime.error.rate / incident detection / 365 days / full for errors
- telemetry.ingest.lag / pipeline health / 14 days / full
- token.metrics (per-model token counts) / cost & billing reconciliation / 365 days / 1:100 unless customer requires full retention

Sampling guidance:
- Error events: never sampled out.
- High-volume successful requests: sample at 1:10 by default; for compliance customers this can be set to 1:1 with approval.

Pre-handoff checklist (operator-run)

- [ ] Customer-accessible runbook created in customer workspace with: cidr ranges, operator account IDs, expected control-plane endpoints.
- [ ] KMS/HSM handshake validated and documented with crypto-agility test vectors.
- [ ] Telemetry consumer endpoints (customer SIEM / splunk / hosted observability) configured and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Baseline SLOs recorded and synthetic smoke tests executed (30-minute run).
- [ ] Evidence bundle generated: config manifests, signed image digests, package provenance, and a short 5–10 minute video of smoke test run.

Cutover / Handoff procedure (step-by-step)

1) Pre-cutover window (T-60 to T-15 minutes)
   a. Notify stakeholders via prearranged channel and update the deployment incident ticket.
   b. Freeze configuration changes (no CI pushes) for the window.
   c. Take artifacts snapshot: kube manifests, runtime config, model artifact checksums. Store signed bundle in evidence store.

2) Warm state and traffic shadowing (T-15 to T-5 minutes)
   a. Prime KV caches with representative prompt set: run `redwood-tool prime-cache --model <id> --prompts prompts.json`
   b. Start traffic shadowing: duplicate 1% of production traffic to the new target. Monitor latency and error delta over a 5-minute window.

3) Cutover (T0)
   a. Execute traffic cut: update routing policy to route X% to target (example incremental percentages: 10, 25, 50, 100 over 10-minute gates). Use automated gating if running under Canary controller.
   b. Continuously monitor critical signals: request.latency.p95, runtime.error.rate, consumer-endpoint-ack (customer telemetry ack).
   c. If any gating threshold breaches, run the rollback procedure (see below).

4) Final handoff (T+30 to T+120 minutes)
   a. After steady-state observed for 60 minutes at 100% traffic with no regressions, produce a handoff report summarizing metrics vs baseline.
   b. Deliver evidence bundle to customer and run a joint acceptance test.
   c. Change ticket status to 'handoff-complete' and record final artifacts in the evidence ledger.

Gating thresholds and SLO checks (examples)

- Latency: p95 must not exceed baseline + 60ms during each gate.
- Error rate: runtime.error.rate must remain <= baseline * 1.5 or absolute 0.5% (whichever is smaller).
- Telemetry continuity: telemetry.ingest.lag must remain < 3 minutes and consumer endpoint ack must appear within 5 minutes of event generation.

Rollback decision matrix

Immediate rollback triggers (action: roll back to previous routing/state and open postmortem):
- Fatal errors causing > 1% user-facing failures within a 5-minute sliding window.
- KV cache corruption events (> 0.1% of responses with cache-mismatch signature).
- Telemetry blackout: no telemetry ingested for > 5 minutes from the new target.

Soft signals (action: pause, further verification, or partial roll back):
- Latency p95 drift above gating threshold but < 2x threshold: pause and investigate with deeper traces.
- Consumer ack lagging but eventually arriving within 20 minutes: continue with reduced step sizes and notify customer SLA owner.

Rollback procedure (operator steps)

1. Set routing back to last known-good configuration immediately. Example CLI:

   redwood-route update --route id=<route> --target <previous-cluster-id> --weight 100 

2. Halt ongoing canary/gating jobs and mark the release as suspended in the release ledger.

3. Capture forensic evidence: runtime logs (last 30 minutes), model.swap.event entries, and the telemetry ingestion window. Store in evidence store with signed metadata.

4. Notify customer with standardized rollback communication template and next steps.

Evidence preservation and compliance notes

- All evidence bundles must include SHA256 digests of artifacts and be signed by operator PGP key. Keep a retention pointer in the Customer Evidence Ledger for 365 days (or longer per customer contract).
- For regulated customers (finance/healthcare), set telemetry token.metrics retention to 365 days and maintain un-sampled records for the acceptance window.

Operator runbook snippets and commands

- Prime cache example:
  redwood-tool prime-cache --model gpt-redwood-1 --prompts ./smoke/prompts.json --concurrency 8

- Check telemetry ingestion latency (jq pipeline example):
  curl -sS http://telemetry.local/metrics?from=-15m | jq '.[] | select(.name=="telemetry.ingest.lag")'

- Create evidence bundle (example):
  tar czf evidence-$(date +%F-%H%M).tgz ./manifests ./images-digests ./logs && gpg --sign --armor evidence-*.tgz && rclone copy evidence-*.tgz.gpg remote:evidence/customer-123/

Post-handoff validation and day-2 ops notes

- Validate cost accounting: compare token.metrics sampled totals against billing collector. Discrepancies > 0.5% require escalation.
- Schedule a 72-hour validation window: automated synthetic tests run hourly to verify model quality, latency, and cache hit ratios.
- Patch management: field operator should schedule non-breaking, low-risk security patches to control-plane agents during weekly maintenance windows and avoid upgrades within 72 hours of a cutover.

Upgrade and rollback reminders specific to private deployments

- For on-prem air-gapped sites: always verify offline artifact signatures and that operator keys used for signing are present in HSM.
- For VPC-connected private deployments: route control-plane upgrades through a staging control-plane in the same region and run cross-region fallback tests prior to production promotion.

Common failure scenarios and mitigations

- Scenario: Unexpected model quality regression after model swap.
  Mitigation: Immediately revert to previous model variant, collect inference samples for evaluation harness, and open a regression ticket with Applied ML.

- Scenario: Telemetry consumer rejects events due to schema mismatch.
  Mitigation: Enable backpressure queue and forward raw payloads to evidence store while patching the consumer schema adapter.

Appendices

A. Customer Handoff Checklist (short)
- CIDR allowlist entries for operator endpoints
- Operator account (IAM) with minimal privilege roles documented
- KMS/HSM contact and credential exchange timestamped
- Agreed sampling/config retention policy documented and signed
- Acceptance prompt set and test harness access

B. Example minimal telemetry YAML (for operator to share with customer)

telemetry: 
  signals: 
    - name: request.latency
      retention_days: 90
      sample: 1.0
    - name: runtime.error.rate
      retention_days: 365
      sample: 1.0
    - name: token.metrics
      retention_days: 365
      sample: 0.01
  consumer_endpoints:
    - name: customer-splunk
      url: https://splunk.example.com/ingest
      auth: token

C. Templates and links
- Handoff email template (operators/templates/handoff-email.md)
- Evidence manifest format (operators/templates/evidence-manifest.md)
